result.title: From Token-Max to Outcome-Max: How You Use AI Determines Its Productivity
result.summary: Generative artificial intelligence (AI) models can perform increasingly complex tasks, yet greater AI usage does not necessarily translate into proportional productivity gains. We identify token-max as one source of this inefficiency: when token consumption is treated as productive effort, agents are encouraged to over-exert and expend computation beyond what is necessary. We instead propose outcome-max, which rewards independently verified task completion per unit cost and induces a principled stopping rule. Then, to study these objectives, we develop a three-level simulation framework spanning immediate interaction, long-run behavioral adaptation, and organizational collaboration. Across all three levels, outcome-max improves the efficiency of AI-assisted production while largely preserving verified task performance. To further align these incentives with outcome-max, we introduce OutcomeShare, an incentive mechanism. Theory and simulation show that OutcomeShare can induce participation while generating shared gains for employees, firms, and LLM providers. Together, our results suggest that AI productivity not only depends on model capability, but also on how to construct the objectives governing AI use.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出以 token 消耗衡量产出会导致过度计算，提出以「单位成本下经独立验证的任务完成」为目标（outcome-max），并用三层仿真框架研究其对效率、长期行为与组织协作的影响，同时提出 OutcomeShare 激励机制。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「以验证完成度而非 token 量定义目标、并内生诱导停止规则」的表述，可能为 LVR 中 STOP 决策的收益/成本度量与长度泛化评价提供目标层面的概念借鉴，但属经济学仿真，需核查可迁移性。
